closingKeywordWhy: The issue title says 'developer and team'. The maintainer chose team-level only, so the developer half is a deliberate scope decision (spec D1, D13), not a slice of remaining work: nothing further is planned for it, and leaving #619 open would track work nobody intends to do. Everything the spec specifies ships in this PR.

stageDetail.detail: harness:brainstorming loaded and followed inline in an unattended lane. EVALUATE questions were settled by the maintainer's brief (team-only, hard-to-fake signals, Goodhart test, report-only, folder convention) or took the recommended option (assumptions below). Approaches weighed: a self-contained report-only skill (chosen), a ts/src engine command (rejected: history module and perf headroom at zero), and a section inside canary-manhunter (rejected: manhunter is a release dossier with a completeness exit code, and it would mix a gate with a scorecard). The soundness review ran as an inline self-check, not as the separate harness-soundness-review skill. The SKILLS.md advisor scan (advise_skills) was not run. The roadmap row was edited by hand to done in this PR rather than through manage_roadmap promote, per the repo's roadmap sync hazard.

Seven tasks written inline (no harness-planner sub-agent), auto-approved in the unattended lane. No sub-agent of any kind ran: the maintainer capped the session at two concurrent agents and this lane is one of them.

Each task's test file was written and run red (missing module, or failing assertions for the security tests) before its implementation; one commit per task. The task-3 tests were committed red at ef51ab6b during a usage-limit stop, then turned green at 878305f0 before any further push. The Goodhart invariant was proven to bite by planting a share in red-mainline-commits (red commits / commits): the invariant test failed with 0.5 -> 0.2, and the plant was restored from a scratchpad copy.

Three coordinator-relayed findings from an automated commit review, all fixed test-first in 85a4b65c. (1) HIGH, read.mjs followed symlinks and forwarded parse-error messages quoting file bytes: every path, the operator's and each directory entry, is now resolved strictly inside the working directory, each segment lstat'ed from the root down (canary-unquarantine's within() and symlinkOnPath() convention), a symlink is reported as 'not read: symlink', containment is re-checked against the realpath'd root, JSON parse errors report only the error name and position, and filesystem errors report only their code. (2) MEDIUM, the single-file branch of readJsonFiles skipped the prefix and .json gate and treated 'not a directory' as a file: both branches now apply the same gate and anything that is not a regular file is refused. (3) MEDIUM, md() did not stop GFM autolinks: scheme URLs, www. hosts and bare emails are defanged with escaped brackets. Tests cover a symlinked file, a symlinked parent directory, a symlinked directory entry pointing outside the root (not read, no content leaked), a malformed file whose bytes never reach any output, the single-file gate, a non-regular entry, and each autolink trigger.

Measured with harness CLI 14.1.1 in clean detached worktrees of the merge base (ea020e5e) and the head, outside the checkout. Perf: 200 at head vs 200 at base, 0 new findings, ceiling 201 (an earlier head had 1 new coupling finding on scorecard.mjs at 0.86; fixed by splitting the evaluator registry into evaluators.mjs and folding mainline.mjs into suite.mjs). Entropy: 100 at head vs 100 at base, +0 (two dead exports, INPUTS and SCHEMA_VERSION, were found and un-exported). Arch: 0 new violations, 0 regressions; the same 8 pre-existing violations at base and head. Docs coverage: 152/528 at head vs 140/517 at base, 28.79% against the 26.73% floor. No baseline, allowance, ceiling or harness.config.json limit was edited; only entropy.entryPoints and performance.entryPoints gained canary-batgirl/scripts/cli.mjs. The ratchets suggested lowering the entropy ceiling and restamping the docs floor; neither was done here, because a restamp belongs in its own PR measured on clean main.

The full diff was read as a reviewer, with no parallel review agents (harness:code-review's fan-out is excluded by the lane cap). Checked: every input-derived string reaches output only through plain() or md(); JSON keys are constants; no author field is read; every scan is linear and bounded; the evaluators default their limits when none is passed; a single-file target outside the prefix gate is an I/O error. Typecheck findings in the skills project were fixed with JSDoc types (d7f7fff3).

ts/: build, typecheck and format:check pass; npm test passes after the skill-examples fix (a runnable --help example in SKILL.md). agents/skills: typecheck and format:check pass; the batgirl suites pass (88 tests, 98% line coverage across the skill). blackhawk --strict and savant --strict pass over ts/test and agents/skills/test. The full skills suite's only failures across runs were 30 s timeouts in canary-unquarantine-trial.test.ts while a second lane loaded the machine; that file passed in isolation, and the change does not touch canary-unquarantine.

assumptions: Six dimensions, chosen and rejected as listed in the spec's 'Signals considered' tables, each rejected signal with its cheapest gaming path.
No composite score: an average over assessed dimensions rises when a bad dimension's input is withheld (spec D3).
Counts, not shares, wherever the denominator is cheap to pad: vacuous tests, unexplained switch-offs, red mainline commits (spec D4).

The escape log (manhunter's .canary/escapes.json) gains an optional caught array as the escaped-defect ratio's denominator. Verified that its only other reader, ts/src/analysis/manhunter/escapes.ts, ignores unknown keys; a test in ts/test/manhunter-sections.test.ts pins it.
Coverage-verified share is measured per changed unit (sum of unitsMatched over sum of unitsTotal), not per finding, because the finding share rises when untested code is added under coverage.
One batwoman report per issue; duplicates are counted and printed, never scored (spec D11).
The mainline branch defaults to main and is set with --branch.
Limits: 32 MiB per file, 100 000 entries, 200 000 history lines, 500 files per directory. An input over a limit is not read and not partly scored.

A named input that is missing, outside the working directory or not a regular file exits 1; a default path that is absent, a symlink, an oversized input or an unparseable file makes its dimension not assessed with the reason.
No standalone ADR: D1 and D2 are maintainer decisions recorded in the spec, and D3 and D4 are design rules local to this skill.
--out follows the canary-ivy and canary-question convention and is not contained to the working directory: it is the operator's chosen destination.
deviations: Permission-hygiene slip: during task 1 the vitest.config.ts coverage include and the package.json format glob were edited with a python3 heredoc through Bash, against the rule that files are written only with the Write and Edit tools. The edit itself was correct and is in commit 44f00063. No settings or allowlist file was touched by this lane; whether a permission prompt for it was approved could not be verified from inside the session.

The Write tool turned \u escapes for non-ASCII characters into literal characters; they were converted back to ASCII escapes with an in-place perl substitution before each commit, and every skill source and test file is ASCII.
The lane was stopped once by a usage limit (WIP pushed at ef51ab6b with a deliberately red test) and resumed on the coordinator's instruction.
